content_voiceover: This slide summarizes the safety profile from ASC4FIRST at week ninety six, comparing asciminib, imatinib, and second generation TKIs. Grade three or higher adverse events occurred in forty four point five percent of asciminib patients, compared with forty nine point five percent on imatinib and fifty nine point eight percent on second generation TKIs, so asciminib had the lowest rate of severe toxicity. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation followed the same pattern, only five percent with asciminib versus thirteen point one percent with imatinib and twelve point seven percent with second generation TKIs. Dose adjustments or interruptions were needed in thirty three percent of asciminib patients versus forty one point four and fifty seven point eight percent respectively. Statistically, the hazard ratio for time to treatment discontinuation due to adverse events, asciminib versus second generation TKIs, was zero point four six, meaning a fifty four percent lower risk of stopping treatment because of toxicity. Combined with the efficacy data from the previous slide, this favorable tolerability profile is asciminib's key selling point as first line therapy.
keypoints: Grade 3 or higher AEs lowest with asciminib at 44.5 percent
AE driven discontinuation only 5 percent with asciminib, versus 13 percent with TKIs
Fifty four percent lower risk of AE related discontinuation versus 2G TKIs
Asciminib pairs better efficacy with meaningfully better tolerability
keypoint_voiceover: The safety data reinforce the efficacy story. Asciminib consistently caused fewer severe adverse events, fewer discontinuations, and fewer dose interruptions than either imatinib or second generation TKIs. The fifty four percent reduction in AE driven discontinuation risk versus second generation TKIs is the number to remember for boards.
